question: Name WHY each panel realm holds its own script source: re-fetched and re-compiled per iframe, retained after teardown, or both.
answer: BOTH, and the split is now measured. Four realms each compile their own copy (61.74 MB redundant of 86.78 MB held), and the copies of destroyed realms are still reachable after a forced GC. One generation of dead realms is retained, NOT one per cycle.
config: deployed, PO workload, 4 DISTINCT symbols @1m, forced-GC floors, 3 cycles
cycleCountIsThreeOnPurpose: A heap snapshot serializes to ~2.3x usedJSHeapSize and JSON.parse dies above V8 max string length (0x1fffffe8). 3 cycles -> 305 MB snapshot, parses. 6 cycles -> ~560 MB, parse failure. All numbers below are 3 cycles; nothing is truncated.

instrument.name: SCRIPT-REALM-CENSUS-V1
instrument.whyNeeded: aggregateRetainerPaths() normalizes `system / Script / <url>` down to `system / Script`, so it can report that script source retains mass but cannot say whether a file is held once or once per realm. Copy count per URL is the measurement that separates 'compiled once and shared' from 'compiled per iframe and kept'.
instrument.snapshotReuse: --snapshot-out=<path> writes the raw CDP snapshot buffer to disk (no JS string is materialized), so one 7-minute run can be re-analyzed offline without re-driving the browser.

partA_compiledPerRealm.finding: 53 shared module URLs are present EXACTLY 4 times — one per panel iframe. 5 more are present 3 times.
partA_compiledPerRealm.whyNotACacheBustingBug: All four copies carry the identical URL including ?v=20260729b99. HTTP may well serve three of them from cache; V8 still compiles the source once per realm and holds its own source string. Re-fetch is not the cost, per-realm compilation is.
partA_compiledPerRealm.corroboration: The compiled-code family grows with it: InstructionStream +10.51 MB / +5207 objects, BytecodeArray +2.22 MB, FeedbackVector +1.42 MB, ScopeInfo +0.49 MB, (script line ends) +2.07 MB.
partA_compiledPerRealm.peerOnlyScripts: panel-cmd-bridge.js and sync-bridge.js only ever execute inside peer iframes, which is why they read 3 and not 4.

partB_retainedAfterTeardown.finding: The run ends collapsed to a single chart, so ONE live realm — yet 4 copies of every shared module and 3 copies of both peer-only scripts survive the forced GC that precedes the snapshot.
partB_retainedAfterTeardown.cleanestProof: sync-bridge.js runs ONLY inside a chart iframe. Every peer iframe had been destroyed. All 3 copies are still reachable.
partB_retainedAfterTeardown.corroboration: detachedDiv 523 at end of run: detached DOM from the same destroyed panels is also still reachable.

partC_theReferenceThatHoldsThem.howObtained: Raw retainer walk (no path normalization) over the 12 largest ExternalStringData nodes.
partC_theReferenceThatHoldsThem.dominantChain: system / ExternalStringData <- string(source text) <- system / Script / <url> <- system / SharedFunctionInfo / <fn> <- closure <fn> <- Window [JSGlobalObject] (own property <fn>) <- system / NativeContext <- closure DOMTokenList (context) <- system / FunctionTemplateInfo (WeakMap value) <- (Eternal handles)
partC_theReferenceThatHoldsThem.namedCut: Each destroyed realm's global object still carries own properties naming module-level functions, which makes that module's Script — and therefore its whole source string — reachable from the realm's global. Observed property names, one per top file: `_resolveSltpStepperSeedPrice` (order-manager.js), `cb01MountSigV1Enabled` (chart.js), `talariaBuildOverlayBandLegendTokens` (chart-indicators-full.js), `__rebuildObjectsTree` (talaria-v9-live.js). The realm's NativeContext is itself pinned from (Eternal handles) through FunctionTemplateInfo -> WeakMap -> a DOMTokenList closure.
partC_theReferenceThatHoldsThem.instrumentAttributableChains: 2 of the 12 route through `(Global handles) / DevTools console` and through Error.stack (ErrorStackData -> StackTraceInfo -> StackFrameInfo -> Script). Those are my own CDP session and retained Error objects. A should NOT chase those two; they are mine, not the product's.
partC_theReferenceThatHoldsThem.forManagerA: The killable thing named here is the window-property -> closure -> SharedFunctionInfo -> Script edge inside a torn-down panel realm, plus whatever keeps that realm's NativeContext alive. This is a different mechanism from the four orphan listeners already shipped.

correctionToW76.whatIClaimed: W76-P2B read the baseline-to-end-of-run growth census and reported script source + compiled code as the attribution for the ~23 MB/cycle leak.
correctionToW76.whyThatWasWrong: That diff spans a 1-realm baseline against a 4-realm end state, so the one-time cost of standing up four panel realms was counted as if it were per-cycle retention.
correctionToW76.theDisproof: Copies do not accumulate. After 3 cycles the shared modules read x4, not the x10 that retaining every generation would produce. Per-realm script source is therefore a BOUNDED ~62 MB, not a per-cycle term.
correctionToW76.whatStands: The 61.74 MB of redundant per-realm source is real, measured, and worth fixing for peak memory. Cache-shaped retention is still refuted (cache-suspect 65 bytes).
correctionToW76.whatIsNowOpenAgain: The monotonic ~23 MB/cycle is NOT attributed. Do not let A cut for it on the strength of W76-P2B.
correctionToW76.nextMeasurement: Diff two snapshots taken at the SAME collapsed state — after cycle N and after cycle N+1 — instead of baseline vs final. That removes the warm-up term by construction, exactly as the steady-state retention split did for the floors.
